subject: On-prem SLA carveout & shared-responsibility request — SnowPeak Analytics
messages:
From: Michael Stone <michael.stone@snowpeak.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@snowpeak.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA carveout for on-prem VPC deployment

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. We are starting the procurement loop and have a specific ask from our infrastructure team. Because SnowPeak will host the Redwood runtime in our VPC (on-prem equivalent colo + private peering), we need a limited SLA carveout that acknowledges the customer-controlled infra portion of the stack. Specifically: 

- Request: Redwood to accept an SLA that excludes downtime attributable to customer-managed network/storage/hardware and scheduled maintenance windows we control.
- Latency: We want a commitment for service-level latency up to the network edge (i.e., from Redwood’s inference service to the peering endpoint), but network hops inside our colo will be our responsibility.
- Evidence: Our auditors will require a short addendum describing the shared responsibility boundaries.

Attached is a short PDF that summarizes the ask. Can your team provide an addendum or suggested language we can circulate to procurement/legal?

Thanks,
Michael Stone
Head of Infrastructure, SnowPeak Analytics
[attachment: SnowPeak-SLA-exception-request.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Stone <michael.stone@snowpeak.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for on-prem VPC deployment

Michael — thanks for the clear summary and the pdf. Adding Diego (Product Ops) and Karthik (Legal/Contracts) to this thread to draft appropriate language. High-level thoughts: we can accept a carveout that clarifies customer-controlled networking/storage/hardware, and provide an SLA that covers Redwood-managed runtime availability and latency up to the peering endpoint. We typically require a connectivity diagnostics playbook and a joint ops runbook as conditions for any on-prem SLA to ensure triage boundaries are clear.

I’ll coordinate a short addendum draft (1 page) and a runbook checklist for your infra team to sign off on. Can you confirm your expected maintenance windows, and whether you will require punitive credits or just a non-credit formal exception?

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Stone <michael.stone@snowpeak.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for on-prem VPC deployment

On Thu, Mar 19, 2026 at 08:27 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Michael — thanks for the clear summary and the pdf. Adding Diego (Product Ops) and Karthik (Legal/Contracts) to this thread to draft appropriate language.

Michael — a couple operational clarifications from Product Ops: 

- Typical Redwood scope we can guarantee: runtime process availability, model-serving containers, KV cache integrity, and latency from our egress point to the configured peering endpoint.
- We cannot guarantee downstream path (customer LAN, middleboxes, on-prem load balancers) or customer storage performance and will explicitly exclude those.
- We require a signed joint runbook that includes: primary/secondary peering IPs, expected throughput and P95 latency targets at the peering point, escalation contacts, and agreed maintenance blackout windows.

I attached a short draft addendum and runbook template — please review and comment. If SnowPeak is okay with the runbook items we can feed this to Legal for an SLA addendum.

[attachment: redwood_sla_addendum_draft_v1.docx]

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Product Ops Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Stone <michael.stone@snowpeak.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for on-prem VPC deployment

Michael,

Thanks for the draft and Diego’s runbook. From Legal’s perspective we can proceed with a limited SLA addendum that: 

1) Defines the service boundary: Redwood is responsible for the inference runtime and network up to the peering endpoint described in the runbook. Customer is responsible for any infrastructure under their control, including but not limited to LAN, load balancers, storage systems, and physical hardware.
2) Maintenance and scheduled windows under customer control are excluded from Redwood SLA uptime/credit calculations.
3) Any latency SLOs will be defined as measured at the peering endpoint under agreed test traffic patterns; if SnowPeak introduces additional network elements, those will be explicitly excluded.
4) Exception term: this addendum will be a contract exhibit for the term of the Redwood subscription for SnowPeak, subject to a quarterly review.

If SnowPeak requires financial credits for Redwood-side incidents that materially exceed agreed targets, Legal will need to review on a case-by-case basis; our default is to limit credits for on-prem deployments where elements outside Redwood’s control exist.

Please confirm you accept the above in principle and whether you want the addendum to include a fixed credit formula or non-financial remedies (service prioritization, SOC audit support). I can push a redlined exhibit to DocuSign once we agree.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
From: Michael Stone <michael.stone@snowpeak.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@snowpeak.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for on-prem VPC deployment

Karthik, Hannah, Diego — that language looks reasonable and addresses our auditors’ concerns. A couple of quick replies: 

- We prefer a non-credit remedy for now (service prioritization + quarterly joint ops review), but will reserve the right to reopen credits if we see repeated material incidents.
- Confirmed: our maintenance windows are Mon 02:00–04:00 local and we will add a 6-hour pre-notice requirement for anything outside that window.
- I’ll review the runbook template with my infra lead and return redlines by EOD Thursday.

If you can push the redlined exhibit to DocuSign after your internal review, we’ll aim to sign next week. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

— Michael
Head of Infrastructure, SnowPeak Analytics
